messages:
Alex Carter: heads-up — p99 for /v1/chat/generate spiked from ~180ms to ~2.1s around 09:12 PT. Only affects some tenants and mostly short prompts. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/abc123 :warning:
Priya Nair: yup got the alert. looking at kv/prefix cache metrics now, seeing miss rate jump and eviction storms on node pool gp2-us-west-2-a :eyes:
Priya Nair: kcache-stats dump (excerpt):
```
prefix_cache.entries: 124012
prefix_cache.max_entries: 125000
prefix_cache.evictions/min: 420
prefix_cache.miss_rate: 0.74
kv_hits: 1821
kv_misses: 5098
hotkey_counts: {"tenant_9": 1842}
```
Mateo Ruiz: that miss_rate is brutal. eviction/min 420 — looks like thrash. Do we have hotkey detection firing? hotkey_counts shows tenant_9 high, but keys look variable length.
Jia Chen: reproducer I used (from a javaclient loop) reproduces the high tail in ~30s:
```
for i in 1..2000:
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"user: hi\nassistant:" + random_suffix() }'
```
Jia Chen: the random_suffix generator was appending inconsistent whitespace/punctuation which produced many distinct prefixes.
Alex Carter: suspect prefix key normalization bug — if tiny differences create new prefix entries we'll overflow the prefix cache quickly. Any evidence of normalization mismatch between router and engine?
Priya Nair: checking logs... found cases where router stored prefix keys with trailing spaces, engine canonicalized differently so cache misses skyrocketed. snippet from router log:
```
[router] prefix_key="user: order status  " tenant=tenant_9
[engine] prefix_key="user: order status" tenant=tenant_9
```
Mateo Ruiz: that explains it. Keys duped by whitespace. Short-term mitigation: 1) roll out prefix normalization at router layer (trim/collapse whitespace) 2) increase cache capacity by 20% on affected pool 3) enable LFU eviction to keep popular prefixes. Which can we ship quickly?
Priya Nair: I can bump pool config for gp2-us-west-2-a to max_entries=150000 for now and flip eviction policy to LFU in canary. Doing that on canary pool first.
Priya Nair: canary change applied to gp2-us-west-2-a-canary: max_entries=150000, eviction=LFU — monitoring now. :rocket:
sre-bot: canary deploy started by priya — change-id: cfg-3491 — /deploy/status cfg-3491
Priya Nair: initial canary stats after 10m: p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 320ms, miss_rate down to 0.12, evictions/min -> 18. Will keep observing.
Mateo Ruiz: nice. For long-term: we should add deterministic canonicalization (trim, normalize whitespace, optionally hash long prefixes), add server-side hotkey mitigation (route hotkeys to sticky-hotpool), and add an alert for prefix_entropy spike.
Jia Chen: opened issue: https://issues.redwood/internal/INC-7892 "prefix key normalization + hotkey pool" — assigned to eng-runtime, priority P1. Added repro and kcache dump.
Alex Carter: plan: (1) keep canary for 2 hours, (2) if stable, roll to prod pool, (3) ship router normalization patch as hotfix (small change) and (4) schedule follow-up that implements hotpool routing and LFU by default. I'll create the rollout PR.
Priya Nair: +1. Also adding a short-term guard in router to collapse whitespace for any prefix > 128 chars.
Mateo Ruiz: will draft the canonicalization RFC and perf test. We should also add unit test that simulates trailing-space duplication.
Jia Chen: noted. I'll update the incident thread and ping CS for tenant_9. Can we offer them an ETA? After prod roll we should have <500ms p99. I'll tell them 3h tentative.
Alex Carter: thanks all. if p99 creeps back up after prod rollout we'll run a postmortem. For now monitor for regressions and watch prefix_entropy metric. :thumbsup:
